acceptance_criteria: Schedule admission proves the selected runtime transport can execute the requested content type before inserting a pending row.
Supported non-Baileys text schedules use the transport's canonical text-send method rather than a Baileys raw payload.
Unsupported schedule requests fail synchronously with no durable pending row and no retry budget consumption.
Fire-time capability drift is classified as permanent or operator-actionable rather than transiently retried.
MCP and HTTP admission enforce the same transport-capability contract.
Tests cover Twilio, Signal, iMessage, and Baileys text admission plus unsupported media.
blast_radius: Every scheduled message on Twilio, Signal, or iMessage, including one-shot and recurring row state, retry budgets, operator alerts, HTTP and MCP admission, and misleading pending status.

No decisive or affected path changed from that audited main. Observed exact-main HTTP and MCP paths share an enqueue helper that validates payload shape but receives no runtime transport or capability input. Observed scheduler text execution always calls sendRaw. Observed Twilio, Signal, and iMessage bridges all reject sendRaw, and the scheduler's general failure path resets the row to pending until its retry budget is spent. falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The finding would be falsified if admission rejected unsupported runtime transports or the scheduler delegated text to a supported transport-neutral send. Exact-main source does neither. Product policy must still decide whether each non-Baileys transport supports scheduled text or should reject it before persistence.
impact: Users receive a successful durable schedule admission on non-Baileys runtimes even though the fire-time bridge rejects the only method the scheduler calls, causing deterministic retries, delayed failure, and possible recurring-occurrence skips.
lead_verification_obligations: Re-read issue #2554 and remote main before integration.
Reconfirm the shared enqueue path, scheduler text seam, and every non-Baileys bridge capability.
Choose and document support policy for scheduled text and media per transport.
Add RED admission and fire-time tests for Twilio, Signal, iMessage, and Baileys.
Prove unsupported requests create no row and consume no retry count.
Run pinned scheduler, health schedule, MCP scheduling, bridge, and database suites on committed bytes.
